Same crash, same film. Change one word in a question, and people remember broken glass that was never there.
In 1974, Elizabeth Loftus and John Palmer showed students car-crash films and asked how fast the cars were going.
Only the verb changed. 'Smashed' got an average of about 41 miles per hour. 'Hit' got 34.
Some crashes were staged at known speeds, yet the guesses barely followed. The word mattered more.
In a second test, a week after the same question, students were asked: did you see any broken glass?
There was none. Yet 16 of 50 in the 'smashed' group said yes. In the 'hit' group, 7.
The researchers' explanation: what you saw and what you were told later blend into one memory.
Memory isn't a recording. Have you ever remembered something that turned out wrong?
